issues.description: The solution declares Genre properties as private (private let name, private let subgenre) but the Client implementation accesses genre.name and genre.subgenre from another source file. In Swift, private restricts access to the declaring source file, so Client.swift cannot access these properties and the code will not compile. The problem statement describes Genre as having a name and optional subgenre (implying they should be usable when printing the inventory), and the example Client code expects direct access. This is a visibility mismatch between the solution and the intended API described in the problem statement and used by Client.
issues.suggested_fix: Make Genre's stored properties accessible from other files in the module. For example, remove the 'private' access modifiers so they are internal by default (e.g. 'let name: String' and 'let subgenre: String?'), or mark them 'public' if the intent is wider visibility. This preserves the intended design (immutable let properties) and allows Client.swift to read genre.name and genre.subgenre when printing the inventory.
